smell_validity.evidence: The three values are literally the existing settings.Domain record's fields, still used as a unit elsewhere; five signatures across two packages re-declare them as unrelated pieces, and a partial domain is unusable. With the healthy record coexisting and the recently added Provider field showing the ripple cost, the eroded-record fault is unmistakable unlabeled.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Any new domain field—the multi-provider feature just added one—forces signature edits across the flow, manager, validation and tests. Provider-ownership policy now lives in two field-level copies that must agree, so the erosion is a lasting trap whose removal restores a real ownership boundary, though benefit stays confined to one flow.

development_plausibility.evidence: A 'stop leaning on the settings model' field-passing refactor is an idiomatic, believable follow-up to the real multi-provider feature, keeping style, error semantics and tests intact. Weakness: the same sweep reshapes a separate package's validation, copying the field style beyond the stated motive—plausible, faintly regular/task-shaped.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names every site, pins preserved behavior (fallback order, cache advance, RunOnce exit, validation outcomes) and out-of-scope surfaces, and allows the existing record or an equivalent type. It explicitly blocks realistic near-misses—dangling field-level shims, partial cleanup, feature or config-format redesign—materially preventing costly wrong directions.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Several purposes: dispatch signatures, provider-resolution with fallback absorption, orchestration hand-off (goroutine, RunOnce), startup validation and test calls. Validation must keep config context and exact outcomes; resolution must keep the effective-name result while absorbing the fallback—distinct decisions beyond one regrouping rule, but dispatch and tests stay uniform, blocking 5.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt itself enumerates the complete scope—manager fan-out, update engine, provider resolution, the fallback helper, startup validation, and test call sites. Verification that no other callers exist is routine confirmation, not discovery; no undisclosed location needs finding.

repair_coordination.evidence: Parameter reintroduction must land simultaneously across the manager, flow signatures, resolution, validation and tests. The shared rule—one authoritative provider answer—breaks silently if the handler adopts it while validation keeps its inline fallback copy, leaving duplicable stale policy; no evidence of two genuinely interacting behavioral rules (timing, resources).

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule—re-thread the existing record through every signature, resolve the provider from it via the authoritative accessor, delete leftover shims, adapt call sites—covers essentially all locations without per-location behavioral decisions; the needed choices are global, not location-specific.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong fallback re-implementation compiles and passes the shown tests, which assert only loop cancellation and concurrent shutdown: mixed multi-provider configs get misrouted updates or mislabeled notifications. Validation-copy drift similarly hides until misconfigured startup. Two distinct hidden paths, one visibly unchecked; no stage/state interaction shown.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
